title: Identification of Fasudil as a collaborator to promote the anti-tumor effect of lenvatinib in hepatocellular carcinoma by inhibiting GLI2-mediated hedgehog signaling pathway.
authors: Huang, Yilan; Wang, Siwei; Zhang, Xiaojun; Yang, Chen; Wang, Sikai; Cheng, Hongxia; Ke, Aiwu; Gao, Chao; Guo, Kun
one_liner_zh: 该文研究肝癌中仑伐替尼耐药机制及药物联用策略，核心为信号通路与药物筛选，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: Lenvatinib is a frontline tyrosine kinase inhibitor for patients with advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). However, just 25% of patients benefit from the treatment, and acquired resistance always develops. To date, there are neither effective medications to combat lenvatinib resistance nor accurate markers that might predict how well a patient would respond to the lenvatinib treatment. Thus, novel strategies to recognize and deal with lenvatinib resistance are desperately needed. In the current study, a robust Lenvatinib Resistance index (LRi) model to predict lenvatinib response status in HCC was first established. Subsequently, five candidate drugs (Mercaptopurine, AACOCF3, NU1025, Fasudil, and Exisulind) that were capable of reversing lenvatinib resistance signature were initially selected by performing the connectivity map (CMap) analysis, and fasudil finally stood out by conducting a series of cellular functional assays in vitro and xenograft mouse model. Transcriptomics revealed that the co-administration of lenvatinib and fasudil overcame lenvatinib resistance by remodeling the hedgehog signaling pathway. Mechanistically, the feedback activation of EGFR by lenvatinib led to the activation of the GLI2-ABCC1 pathway, which supported the HCC cell's survival and proliferation. Notably, co-administration of lenvatinib and fasudil significantly inhibited IHH, the upstream switch of the hedgehog pathway, to counteract GLI2 activation and finally enhance the effectiveness of lenvatinib. These findings elucidated a novel EGFR-mediated mechanism of lenvatinib resistance and provided a practical approach to overcoming drug resistance in HCC through meaningful drug repurposing strategies.
abstract_zh: 乐伐替尼（lenvatinib）是晚期肝细胞癌（HCC）患者的一线酪氨酸激酶抑制剂。然而，仅25%的患者从治疗中获益，且获得性耐药总是发生。迄今为止，既没有有效药物来对抗乐伐替尼耐药，也没有准确标志物可预测患者对乐伐替尼治疗的反应程度。因此，迫切需要识别和处理乐伐替尼耐药的新策略。在本研究中，首先建立了一个稳健的乐伐替尼耐药指数（LRi）模型，用于预测HCC中乐伐替尼的反应状态。随后，通过执行连接图谱（CMap）分析，初步筛选出五种能够逆转乐伐替尼耐药特征的候选药物（巯嘌呤、AACOCF3、NU1025、法舒地尔和依昔舒林），并通过一系列体外细胞功能实验和异种移植小鼠模型，法舒地尔最终脱颖而出。转录组学揭示，乐伐替尼与法舒地尔联合给药通过重塑刺猬（hedgehog）信号通路克服了乐伐替尼耐药。机制上，乐伐替尼对EGFR的反馈激活导致GLI2-ABCC1通路激活，从而支持HCC细胞的存活和增殖。值得注意的是，乐伐替尼与法舒地尔联合给药显著抑制了刺猬通路的上游开关IHH，以抵消GLI2激活，最终增强乐伐替尼的疗效。这些发现阐明了乐伐替尼耐药的一种新型EGFR介导机制，并通过有意义的药物再利用策略，为克服HCC中的药物耐药提供了实用方法。
